verses.text: A man from Ephraim’s hill country was named Micah. 🌿
He told his mother, ‘That 1,100 pieces of silver someone took from you—the ones you cursed about? I have the silver. I took it.’ His mother said, ‘May Yahweh bless you, my son!’ 💬
Micah returned the 1,100 pieces to his mother. She said, ‘I’m setting this silver apart for Yahweh, for my son, to make a carved image and a metal statue. Now I’m giving it back to you.’ 💰
When he gave the silver back, his mother took two hundred pieces and gave them to a silversmith, who made a carved image and a cast-metal statue. They were kept in Micah’s house. 🪙
Micah had a shrine of his own. He made an ephod and household idols, then appointed one of his sons as priest. 🏠
Back then, Israel had no king. Everyone just did whatever seemed right to them. ⚖️
There was a young Levite from Bethlehem in Judah, from Judah’s clan, living there. 🌿
He left Bethlehem in Judah, looking for somewhere else to settle. On his journey he came to Micah’s house in Ephraim’s hill country. 🧳
Micah asked him, ‘Where are you coming from?’ He said, ‘I’m a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah, looking for a place to live.’ 🗣️
Micah told him, ‘Stay with me. Be like a father and a priest to me, and I’ll pay you ten silver pieces a year, give you clothes, and feed you.’ So the Levite moved in. 🤝
The Levite was happy to stay with Micah, and the young man became like one of Micah’s sons. 🏠
Micah appointed the Levite as priest, and he lived in Micah’s house. 🙏
Micah said, ‘Now I know Yahweh will bless me, because I have a Levite as my priest.’ 🙌
